title: Audit selected-SDK profile and content mount isolation
goal: Establish the actual selected SDK filesystem's bounded isolation and read-only behavior before profile/save integration, using original game-free host trees and the verified library package.
acceptance: Use original fixtures and the actual dynamically loaded selected-SDK filesystem module; record exact SDK/source/compiler/library identities, API semantics and the boundary between host mount policy and unverified guest save services

Exercise independent profile filesystems with the same guest path, persistent independent payloads, shared read-only content, invalid/traversing paths, relative directory operations, rename/remove permissions and symlink/reparse escape probes where supported

Keep every file, link and outside-root canary inside a private per-attempt synthetic tree; verify denied operations preserve canary/content/other-profile bytes and retain unsupported-host skips without touching owned game content or existing saves

Retain baseline failures and require exact wrong-result/incomplete-process rejection; publish an actionable SDK-repair or integration handoff for demonstrated gaps rather than patching shared code or treating a passing subset as secure save support
validation: Run isolated and repeated case orders on native Windows/Linux and supported host sanitizers against the same verified SDK profile; explicitly identify uninstrumented library coverage
Record bounded fixture-operation timing over at least three processes, output/mutation checks and exact public check commands; do not infer gameplay performance or console save compatibility

Change only this reserved diagnostic lane and its task metadata; no SDK, preparation cache, runtime/storage interface, controller model, allocation imports, shared startup harness or service admission changes
size: bounded game-free filesystem investigation; split demonstrated repairs
